title: Homotopy density of small presentable cofibrant objects
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A model category is combinatorial when its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems have small generating sets. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Locally $\lambda$-presentable means generated under these colimits by a small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. Use homotopy colimits of [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags], computed by the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial and let $\lambda$ be an infinite regular cardinal such that $\mathcal M$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable, $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserve objectwise weak equivalences, and there is a functorial cofibrant replacement preserving $\lambda$-presentable objects. Choose a small full representative category $C$ of the cofibrant $\lambda$-presentable objects. For each $X\in\mathcal M$, let $(C\downarrow X)$ have objects $(c,u:c\to X)$ and arrows $a:c\to c'$ with $u'a=u$, and let $V_X(c,u)=c$. Then the canonical augmentation
$$\operatorname{hocolim}_{(C\downarrow X)}V_X\longrightarrow X$$
is a weak equivalence. The assertion holds for all $X$, without a fibrancy assumption.

source.place: Proposition 4.7 and its proof, printed p. 187, stated with the three explicit sufficient cardinal hypotheses used in that proof. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-density result. Sources read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-canonical-density] to the underlying category of $\mathcal M$ at the given $\lambda$. Choose a small full category $B$ of representatives of all $\lambda$-presentable objects, taking its cofibrant representatives to be exactly the already specified $C$. Such a choice is possible because cofibrancy is invariant under isomorphism: the initial map is transported by that isomorphism, and cofibrations are a lifting class. Set $I=(B\downarrow X)$ and $J=(C\downarrow X)$, and put $U(b,u)=b$. Both categories are small: their object sets are small unions of the small sets $\operatorname{Hom}(b,X)$, and their arrow sets are subsets of the corresponding small Hom sets of $B$. The inclusion of $B$ into the full category of all presentable objects induces an equivalence of comma categories, with inverse obtained by replacing each domain by its chosen representative and conjugating arrows. Under this equivalence a cocone is exactly the same family of maps after those isomorphisms; cocone factorization and uniqueness, and the existence of cocones on diagrams of size less than $\lambda$, therefore transfer in both directions. The cited leaf gives that $I$ is $\lambda$-filtered and that the actual canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_I U\to X$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Remark 2.5 and Proposition 4.7(i), printed pp. 181, 188; representative and smallness details made explicit.

proof.text: Let $p_I:Q_IU\to U$ be a projective cofibrant replacement as in [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags]. Choose it by the functorial factorization of the initial diagram map as a projective cofibration followed by a projective trivial fibration. Thus $p_I$ is an objectwise trivial fibration, in particular an objectwise weak equivalence. Since $I$ is small and $\lambda$-filtered by Step 1, the assumed preservation of objectwise weak equivalences by $\lambda$-filtered colimits applies to this particular transformation. Hence $\operatorname{colim}_I p_I$ is a weak equivalence. Composing it with the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_I U\to X$ proves that the canonical augmentation $a_I:\operatorname{hocolim}_I U=\operatorname{colim}_I Q_IU\to X$ is a weak equivalence. This is a direct application of the stated filtered-colimit hypothesis to the definition of homotopy colimit.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.7(i), printed p. 188: compare the projective replacement colimit with the ordinary canonical colimit.

proof.text: Fix the functorial cofibrant replacement $q:Q\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$ in the hypothesis. Use the fixed representative isomorphisms to regard $Q$ on $B$ as a functor $\bar Q:B\to C$: if $\theta_b:\bar Qb\xrightarrow{\sim}Qb$ is the chosen isomorphism, set $\bar Q(t)=\theta_{b'}^{-1}Q(t)\theta_b$ and $\bar q_b=q_b\theta_b$. Thus $\bar q$ is natural and each component is a weak equivalence. The restriction lands in $C$ because $Qb$ is both cofibrant and $\lambda$-presentable, exactly by the two replacement hypotheses. Let $g:J\to I$ be inclusion and define $f:I\to J$ by $f(b,u)=(\bar Qb,u\bar q_b)$ and $f(t)=\bar Q(t)$. The identity $u'\bar q_{b'}\bar Q(t)=u't\bar q_b=u\bar q_b$ checks the required comma relation. The maps $\bar q_b$ give a natural transformation $gf\to\mathrm{id}_I$; restricting them to $c\in C$ gives $fg\to\mathrm{id}_J$, since both endpoints then belong to the full subcategory $C$. After $U$ and $Ug$, respectively, all components of these transformations are the weak equivalences $\bar q_b$ and $\bar q_c$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.7(ii), printed p. 188: the replacement functor, the two comma functors and their natural transformations, with representative transport formulas.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags] to $g:J\to I$, $f:I\to J$, and $U:I\to\mathcal M$. Step 1 verifies smallness, and Step 3 supplies both required natural-transformation zigzags and verifies their weak-equivalence conditions on the actual value diagrams, not merely on indexing nerves. Its conclusion gives that the canonical reindexing map $g_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_J Ug\to\operatorname{hocolim}_I U$ is an isomorphism in the homotopy category, and that an actual comparison representing it is a weak equivalence. Here $Ug=V_X$ exactly.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.7(ii), printed p. 188, application of Proposition A.4 and Remark A.5, printed pp. 199-200.

proof.text: Check compatibility with the augmentation using an actual comparison. Write $p_J:Q_J(Ug)\to Ug$ for a projective cofibrant replacement. The pullback $g^*p_I:g^*Q_IU\to Ug$ is an objectwise trivial fibration, hence a projective trivial fibration by the objectwise definitions of projective fibrations and weak equivalences in [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags]. Lift $p_J$ against this map using projective cofibrancy of $Q_J(Ug)$ and the model lifting axiom of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], to obtain $\ell:Q_J(Ug)\to g^*Q_IU$ with $g^*p_I\ell=p_J$. Taking its colimit and then the ordinary reindexing map gives a representative $k:\operatorname{colim}_J Q_J(Ug)\to\operatorname{colim}_I Q_IU$ of $g_*$. On every component $(c,u)$, its composite with $a_I$ is $u(p_J)_{(c,u)}$ by this lifting equality, so the colimit universal property gives the strict equality $a_Ik=a_J$, the canonical augmentation of the item. Step 4 makes $k$ a weak equivalence, Step 2 makes $a_I$ one, and two-out-of-three makes $a_J$ one. No step required that $X$ be fibrant.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition 4.7(ii), printed p. 188; the commuting augmentation triangle is checked using projective replacements and a lift.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.7(i)-(ii), printed p. 188, expanded using Remark 2.5 and Proposition A.4 / Remark A.5, printed pp. 181, 199-200. Source read online but not archived in literature/. The fixed-cardinal density input is the Mathlib leaf; the augmentation triangle is written out with a projective lift.

lean.statement: theorem combinatorial_cofibrant_density (hM : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, w} M) {κ : Cardinal.{w}} [Fact κ.IsRegular] (hLocal : IsCardinalLocallyPresentable M κ) (hfiltered : ∀ (I : Type v) [SmallCategory I] [IsCardinalFiltered I κ] (F G : I ⥤ M) (α : F ⟶ G), (∀ i : I, weakEquivalences M (α.app i)) → weakEquivalences M (colim.map α)) (Q : M ⥤ M) (q : Q ⟶ 𝟭 M) (hqWeak : ∀ X : M, weakEquivalences M (q.app X)) (hqCofibrant : ∀ X : M, IsCofibrant (Q.obj X)) (hqPresentable : ∀ X : M, isCardinalPresentable M κ X → isCardinalPresentable M κ (Q.obj X)) {C : Type v} [SmallCategory C] (ι : C ⥤ M) (hι : ι.FullyFaithful) (hC : ∀ c : C, IsCofibrant (ι.obj c) ∧ isCardinalPresentable M κ (ι.obj c)) (hRepresentative : ∀ Y : M, IsCofibrant Y → isCardinalPresentable M κ Y → ∃ c : C, Nonempty (ι.obj c ≅ Y)) (X : M) (R : ProjectiveHocolimReplacement (M := M) (CostructuredArrow ι X)) : weakEquivalences M (canonicalCofibrantDensityAugmentation ι X R)
lean.note: The helper canonicalCofibrantDensityAugmentation is the actual composite colim(Q_J V_X) -> colim V_X -> X (projective-replacement augmentation followed by the colimit map of the comma arrows), listed so the declaration index assigns it to this node. The comparison category and presentability use the universes of the landed hocolim interface (indexing categories in the hom universe v, presentability cardinals in w); downstream use is at w = v.
